slides.title: Economic Value
slides.text:
Economic Value
Customers get economic value when a product provides tangible monetary savings either at the time of purchase or over its long term use.

slides.title: Strategy
slides.text:
Strategy
A marketing strategy is an overall game plan formulated to achieve long run marketing objectives and meet the needs of a target market.

bullets.text: A marketing strategy is an overall game plan formulated to achieve long run marketing objectives and meet the needs of a target market.

slides.title: Plan
slides.text:
Plan
A marketing plan is the central instrument for directing and coordinating the marketing effort.
A written document that indicates how the firm plans to reach its marketing objective.
For individual products, lines, brands, channels, customer groups.

bullets.text: A marketing plan is the central instrument for directing and coordinating the marketing effort.

slides.title: 1. Defining the Corporate Mission
slides.text:
1. Defining the Corporate Mission
A mission is a clear, concise, and enduring statement of the reasons for an organization’s existence
Often referred to as its core purpose, a company’s mission that provides company employees and management with a shared sense of purpose, direction, and opportunity.

bullets.text: A mission is a clear, concise, and enduring statement of the reasons for an organization’s existence

slides.title: Vision Vs Mission
slides.text:
Vision Vs Mission
A vision statement outlines what an organization aspires to become or achieve in the long-term future. It represents the company's ultimate goal or dream.
A mission statement defines the organization's purpose and primary objectives.

bullets.text: A vision statement outlines what an organization aspires to become or achieve in the long-term future. It represents the company's ultimate goal or dream.

slides.text:
2. Establishing Strategic Business Units
A strategic business unit (S B U):
Is a single business, or a collection of related businesses, that can exist separately from the rest of the company
Has its own set of competitors
Has a manager responsible for strategic planning and profit performance

slides.title: Porter’s 5 Forces Model
slides.text: Porter’s 5 Forces Model
slides.visual_text: Porter's 5 Forces Model, five circles around the centre. Threats of new entrants: how easy is it for new business to set up. Bargaining power (buyers): how much power do customers have. Supplier power: how much power do suppliers have. Threats of substitute: how likely are customers to switch to an alternative. Competitive rivalry: how many companies compete and what is your market share.

slides.title: Overall cost leadership
slides.text:
Overall cost leadership
Firms strive to achieve the lowest production and distribution costs to underprice competitors and win market share.
Emphasis on cost efficient production, economies of scale
Might invite a price war from other competitors and lose out heavily if they rested its whole future on cost alone.

bullets.text: Firms strive to achieve the lowest production and distribution costs to underprice competitors and win market share.

Differentiation
The business concentrates to seek superior performance in an important customer benefit valued by a large segment of the market.
Allows for premium pricing strategy

slides.title: The Organization of the Marketing Plan
slides.text: The Organization of the Marketing Plan
slides.visual_text: The Organization of the Marketing Plan, a stacked chart. Executive Summary: what are the key aspects of the company's marketing plan? Situation Overview: Company (history, culture, resources, offerings, ongoing activities) and Market (key aspects of the markets in which the company competes). Then a group called the G-STIC Action Plan: Goal (Focus: the key performance metric; Benchmarks: the temporal and quantitative criteria for reaching the goal); Strategy (Target Market: target customers, competitors, collaborators, resources and context; Value proposition: the value the offering creates for target customers, collaborators and company stakeholders); Tactics (Market offering: product, service, brand, price, incentives, communication and distribution); Implementation (Development: how the offering is being developed; Deployment: the processes used to bring it to market); Control (Performance: how progress toward the goal is evaluated; Environment: how the company monitors the environment for new opportunities and threats). Last: Exhibits, the details and evidence supporting the action plan.
